newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- China announced plans for retaliatory curbs on U.S. imports.
-- Europe-based Chinese composer Tan Dun said he had been commissioned by the Hong Kong Handover Celebration Committee to compose a symphony for the handover.
-- APPLE DAILY -- An 11-year-old girl who had immigrated to Hong Kong three years ago killed herself by jumping into the sea. It was suspected that it was due to academic pressure.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY -- Tens of thousands of peasants in China's Hunan province rioted in late August over exorbitant levies, taxes and fees set by local officials.
-- MING PAO -- The first gay wedding in Taiwan was attended by more than 600 people, including several government officials.
-- The first music auction in China, scheduled to take place in Xian last week, was called off on orders from Beijing.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- China Pharmaceutical Ent. and Inv. Corp planned to buy in other pharmaceutical factories as well as other businesses in Shijiazhuang.
-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Proposed moves to make small brokers merge into bigger businesses in Hong Kong have encountered sharply divided views.
-- The battle for the multi-billion dollar spoils of China's spectacular economic growth heats up theis week with a visit to Beijing by a high-powered delegation from Europe.
-- English-language HONG KONG STANDARD -- Retired judges are being lured back to work on big-money short-term contracts just months after leaving the judiciary with lucrative payoffs.
